public_rationale: SpartQA documented spatial reasoning tests in April 2021, and PIQA documented physical commonsense tests in November 2019 [e1, e2]. Their existence does not settle whether most forms of spatial and physical reasoning remained untested across all benchmarks on February 17, 2023 [e1, e2]. A December 2023 survey described remaining gaps, but did not establish the extent of coverage at the February date [e3]. These sources also do not settle whether a good, reliable way to measure broad AI commonsense reasoning existed then [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: No supplied audit measures collective benchmark coverage against a defined set of spatial and physical reasoning categories.
Results from individual benchmarks do not establish a reliable measure of broad commonsense reasoning.
The December 2023 survey covers a later inventory and does not quantify how many categories were untested in February 2023.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is no good, reliable way yet to measure AI commonsense reasoning, and most spatial and physical reasoning is untested by existing benchmarks.

statement.excerpt: Important aspects of commonsense reasoning, including most forms of spatial and physical reasoning, remain untested in any of these benchmarks. We do not yet have a good reliable way of measuring how much commonsense reasoning an AI can carry out.

our_interpretation: The coverage assertion concerns the union of existing commonsense benchmarks, not whether each individual benchmark is comprehensive.
Most forms means a majority of meaningful reasoning categories under a defensible taxonomy, rather than a majority of imaginable individual questions.
A good reliable measure means a validated assessment of broad commonsense reasoning that generalizes beyond its particular test items.
The relevant benchmark inventory is the one available on the post date. Individual benchmark scores can be useful without constituting the broad measure claimed to be missing.
criteria.support_condition: An independent coverage audit establishes that the benchmark inventory collectively omits most meaningful spatial and physical reasoning categories, alongside evidence of missing or inadequate validation for broad commonsense measurement.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An independent audit establishes coverage of most relevant categories, or validation establishes an existing reliable broad measure. Evidence for opposing components would warrant mixed rather than a blanket verdict.

evidence.explanation: SpartQA documents substantive spatial reasoning coverage before the post. It rules out an interpretation that spatial reasoning was entirely untested, but does not establish coverage of most forms across the February 2023 inventory.

PIQA provides a concrete physical commonsense dataset with reported human and model performance. Its existence establishes some measurement capability, but not comprehensive category coverage or a validated broad commonsense score.

This independent survey identifies remaining gaps while proposing groups of physical reasoning benchmarks. It concerns a later inventory and does not quantify the claim that most forms were untested in February.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independent audit of benchmarks available on February 17, 2023, using a defensible taxonomy to determine whether most spatial and physical reasoning categories were untested. A separate assessment must establish whether any broad commonsense measure available then met explicit reliability and generalization standards.
